_comment: Bucket policy for the audit WORM archive. Apply with:
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket <ARCHIVE_BUCKET> --policy file://s3-archive-bucket-policy.json
WHY THIS IS NEEDED IN ADDITION TO OBJECT LOCK
Object Lock in COMPLIANCE mode makes an object *version* immutable: a
targeted DeleteObjectVersion is refused outright ('WORM protected'), and no
principal - including the account root - can shorten the retention. That was
verified against the live archive.
What Object Lock does NOT stop is a plain DeleteObject. On a versioned
bucket that call does not remove anything; it writes a zero-byte *delete
marker* that becomes the current version. The locked data version is still
there and still recoverable, so no evidence is destroyed - but a default
ListObjects or GetObject then behaves as though the segment is gone.
For an audit archive that is unacceptable on its own terms: an auditor
listing the bucket would conclude records are missing, and an operator would
have to know to list versions to disprove it. The Deny statements below
remove the possibility rather than relying on nobody exercising it.
Replace ACCOUNT_ID, ARCHIVE_BUCKET and AUDIT_WRITER_ROLE before applying.
DeleteObject is what creates a delete marker; DeleteObjectVersion is
already refused by Object Lock, and denying it here makes the intent
explicit and survives a future retention expiry.
Suspending versioning would break Object Lock's guarantee, and rewriting
retention is the one operation that could shorten the WORM window.
COMPLIANCE mode already blocks the shortening; this also blocks the
attempt being made.
Only the audit service may seal segments. Anyone else writing here could
plant an object that is then permanently undeletable.

operator_notes: Object Lock can ONLY be enabled at bucket creation:
The service logs `worm_archive_misconfigured` at startup if it is missing,
which means archived segments are ordinary deletable objects.
Recovering a segment hidden by a delete marker (if one was created before
Removing a delete marker is permitted and is not a data deletion.
The keyring index is deliberately NOT archived here. Writing wrapped PII
keys into WORM storage would make them undeletable and defeat
crypto-shredding outright - erasure works by destroying that key.
